Thanks, and totally understood. I pulled together a short plan and attached three artifacts we usually provide to procurement/legal up front: a redlined DPA (for faster counter-review), an SCCs mapping checklist, and a current subprocessor snapshot. High level proposal below:  

- Stage 1 (today): Share redlined DPA + SCCs mapping checklist. These address contract and legal mapping questions and let your legal team confirm which SCC clauses apply.  
- Stage 2 (within 48 hours of Stage 1): Provide subprocessor_map_Q2_2025.csv and an operations note describing where EU data is processed (regions, onshore fallbacks). This helps InfoSec validate residency and encryption controls.
- Stage 3: Joint legal call to agree any redline comments. We suggest 1-hour call; Kimberly can lead legal points.
- Stage 4: Final DPA sign via DocuSign and handover to infra for routing configuration.

Notes on TIAs/DTIAs: For pilot traffic that will be routed to EU edge nodes, we provide an optional TIA summary if your team requests transient processing evidence (this is not always required but helps regulated customers). We will include a one-page TIA summary if you want it.

I attached the artifacts as stubs below. Marissa will draft a short mutual action plan and timeline once you confirm the target sign date.
